sections.title: Game2Player: Scaling Gameplay Experience for Visual Agents through Environment-Player Co-Development
sections.abstract: Game2Player co-develops verifiable web-game environments and player agents to produce gameplay training data, reporting improved visual-agent progress on its held-out PlayerBench and the external GameWorld benchmark.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors describe a Builder/Coding Player/VLM Player loop that creates and repairs game tasks, collecting 15.7K trajectories across 568 games and 3,436 tasks; their reported 9B agent raises PlayerBench progress from 14.3% to 31.2% and GameWorld progress from 30.0% to 53.1%.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that generated environments are not guaranteed correct, the pipeline covers offline single-player browser games, the VLM player pauses the game at each decision, and several builder/player models are proprietary.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 19 Hugging Face Daily Papers votes in the 2026-11-19 archive snapshot; highest vote count among selected papers.

sections.title: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate
sections.abstract: Jeveration repurposes a frozen vision-language model and a shared random state for single-pass image generation, image-to-image generation, and dense prediction, reporting 512×512 generation in 78 ms with competitive quality and dense-prediction performance.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors say that conditioning parallel predictions on a shared random state and first learning a distribution over discrete image codes helps maintain global coherence in one-forward-pass generation.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported generation-speed claim is for 512×512 images; the abstract does not establish performance at higher resolutions or in broader deployment settings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 14 Hugging Face Daily Papers votes in the 2026-11-19 archive snapshot; second-highest among selected new submissions.

sections.title: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules
sections.abstract: WorldRuler represents user-defined rules and object state in an executable 3D rule graph and connects rule execution, video generation, and perceptual feedback to preserve and visually realize those rules.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce RuleVerse, built from GTA-V and Habitat interactions, and report experiments on saving/restoring rule-state consistency and realizing rule effects on designated objects and attributes.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evidence is tied to the authors’ RuleVerse data and GTA-V/Habitat pipeline; the abstract does not establish generalization to arbitrary simulators or rule families.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 11 Hugging Face Daily Papers votes in the 2026-11-19 archive snapshot; directly listed in the current cs.AI batch.

sections.title: Code World Model 2.0: Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation
sections.abstract: Invoker-Render pairs bidirectional video creation with a causal four-step streaming renderer conditioned on structural proxies, appearance references, and language, using Progressive Forcing to reduce rollout drift and support long interactive generations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that their four-step renderer outperforms recent streaming baselines on visual quality, structural adherence, and reference preservation, with stable scene and subject appearance in 30-minute racing rollouts.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors identify fixed proxy granularity within rollout windows as a current constraint; dynamic mid-stream level-of-detail changes and closed-loop coupling to interactive state engines remain future work.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 7 Hugging Face Daily Papers votes in the 2026-11-19 archive snapshot; v2 revision falls in the current batch, and the paper reports 140 streaming rollouts.

sections.title: RoughCut-Bench: A Benchmark for Automatic Video Rough-Cut with Large Vision-Language Models
sections.abstract: RoughCut-Bench evaluates visual- and speech-driven video rough-cut workflows with annotated source material and reports that current large vision-language models remain limited at producing expert-aligned cut plans.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors contribute 101 visually driven cases with 831 raw videos and 1,476 highlight annotations, plus 84 transcript-driven cases, along with agentic workflows and evaluation protocols.
sections.unique_caveat: Its evidence is bounded by the benchmark’s 22 films and defined visual/speech-driven cases; the reported model comparisons are not a broad trial of production editing workflows.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 6 Hugging Face Daily Papers votes in the 2026-11-19 archive snapshot; a new cs.CV submission with a benchmark spanning visual and speech-driven editing.
